title: resolveFinalPath infinite-loops on a recorded rename cycle (mv a b; mv b a)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-203 finding (2026-07-25): while building the layered lineage walk, resolveFinalPath (src/reconstruction_lineage.ts) was found to follow the rename chain without a seen-set, so a transcript that records `mv a b` followed by `mv b a` — which real sessions do produce when a rename is undone — makes it loop forever rather than terminating on the cycle. The new layered walk in jfred/src/layered_lineage.ts avoids this by carrying a shared seen-set across both directions, and the engine's version was deliberately left untouched so the fix could be scoped and verified on its own. Add a seen-set (or an explicit cycle error) to resolveFinalPath and every other rename-chain walker that shares the pattern, with a unit test that records the two-hop cycle and asserts termination. No live scenario is known to trigger it yet, so a synthetic fixture is acceptable evidence.

title: renderRevisionText unconditionally appends a trailing newline, so files without one can never blob-match
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-187 finding (2026-07-25): renderRevisionText renders a revision as linesTextOf(rev).join("\n") + "\n" — the trailing newline is unconditional. A file whose real bytes do NOT end in a newline therefore can never hash-match its recorded blob. In the 68-file M sweep this produced a 2/2 correlation: exactly 2 of the 68 baseline blobs lack a trailing newline (docs/design/architecture.md ending 0x2e, docs/design/milestones.md ending 0x2e) and those are exactly the 2 baselineBlobMatched=false rows. The same artifact also corrupts the diskMatched comparison for 3 further files. Fixing this means the engine must carry a 'final line had no newline' bit, which touches the LineEntry vocabulary and every producer/consumer of it — CONFIRM the design with the user before implementing (open question 2 in plans/implementation-notes-tasks-223-224-184-203-207-187.md). Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 187 — the M-file sweep (68 files)".

title: Extend the task-224 seed clamp to the two sibling backup stampers (needs a reproducer first)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-224 follow-up (2026-07-25): task 224 fixed the non-monotonic ladder by giving backup-sourced seeds a two-sided placement window via clampSeedBetweenPreviousAndEdit (jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar.ts), but wired it into ONE proven site — seedStaleEditBases in jfred/src/reconstruction_reseed.ts. Two sibling stampers apply the identical `timestamp: <backupTime>` pattern and therefore share the defect CLASS: backupAfterWriteFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:90-96, used by reversedEditBaseSeed at reconstruction_reseed.ts:157) and backupWritesFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:116-122, used at reconstruction_beacons.ts:158 and via latestBackupWriteFor at reconstruction_beacons.ts:56). They were deliberately NOT changed: completeElidedBeacons and completeTruncatedBeacon are load-bearing for many character-locked scenarios (S27, S28, S30 among others) and already carry their own retiming logic — completeElidedBeacons re-times the BEACON backward when its seed precedes it — so extending the clamp without a reproducer risks breaking locked ground truths to fix a defect nobody has observed. REQUIRE a reproducing scenario that shows one of these two stampers emitting an out-of-order seed BEFORE changing them; then reuse the existing clamp and run the full suite.

title: Layer 1 View: add a File Nav tree to the left of the ruler listing every identified file
description: Layer 1 View feature (2026-07-25, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). Add a File Nav pane on the left, to the LEFT of the sticky ruler gutter, that shows every identified file — including files that were deleted (i.e. files with no current on-disk presence must still be listed). REUSE THE EXISTING FILE NAV COMPONENT the current webapp (index.html) already ships — the user confirmed this 2026-07-25; do NOT write a second tree. The component is already shared by two callers, so a third is the intended extension point: `buildFileTree(files: FileSidebarEntry[]) -> FileTreeNode[]` in jfred/webapp/views/timeline-file-tree.ts (common-prefix stripping, folders-before-files sort, single-child chain collapse) and `renderFileTreeNode(node, callbacks, selectionRoot, coverage?)` in jfred/webapp/views/sidebar.ts (folder = native `<details open>`, leaf = `.file-item` with basename text and full path in `title`, `.file-item.deleted` variant already exists). Existing callers to copy from: views/timeline.ts:211 (the Files sidebar) and views/details.ts:130 (the details pane's "Files touched" tree, which passes no `coverage`). THREE TRAPS. (1) `buildFileTree` consumes `FileSidebarEntry` (timeline-file-tree.ts:13) built by `buildFilesSidebarViewModel` from a `WireTimelineDocument` — Layer 1 has NO such document, so the Layer 1 caller must construct its own `FileSidebarEntry[]`-shaped list from the /api/layer1-view payload (`pairs` + `gitOrphans` + `diskOrphans`), mapping revisionCount to the commit count and isDeleted to a path present in the repo tree but absent on disk; `originalPath` and `renameBadgeLabel` are undefined at Layer 1. (2) The tree's CSS (`.file-folder`, `.file-folder-kids`, `.file-folder-name`, `.file-item`) lives in jfred/webapp/styles.css (20 rules) which layer1.html does NOT load — layer1.html has only an inline `<style>` block, and index.html loads layered-styles.css which carries none of it. Bring the rules across or link the sheet. (3) views/sidebar.ts deliberately MIRRORS `FileSidebarEntry`/`FileTreeNode` rather than importing them (timeline-file-tree.ts imports sidebar.ts, so importing back would be a cycle) — any field added must be added in both places. This pane is the host for the folder-filter behaviour in tasks 253, 254 and 255.

title: Re-center the clicked node in the timeline area that survives after the inspector opens
description: User request 2026-07-25, in their own wording: "when the inspector is displayed, the clicked node should center itself in the displayed timeline area (an area which shrank because the detail view was shown)". Opening the inspector reveals/grows the details pane, which reflows the split and SHRINKS the timeline pane, so the row the user just clicked can end up off-screen or under the pane edge — the click's own target is what they lose sight of. Centering must run against the POST-reflow layout, never the pre-open one. PRIMARY SITE (jfred/webapp): `openNodeInspector` in webapp/views/timeline-render-inspectors.ts:179 — the opener shared by the `{ }` row buttons and DetailsContext.openNodeInspector — calls through to `openInspectorPane` (webapp/inspector.ts:64), which calls `revealDetailsPane()` and thereby shrinks the timeline, but performs NO scroll afterwards. Note its existing comment: it "deliberately does NOT re-call selectTimelineRow ... reopening the selection would loop" — so the fix is a bare re-center of the already-selected row, NOT a selectTimelineRow call, or the loop that comment guards against comes back. Two places already get this right and are the pattern to copy: `selectTimelineRow` (webapp/views/timeline-render-selection.ts:33) ends with `row.scrollIntoView({ block: "center" })` AFTER awaiting the details render ("item 50"), and the `/at/<n>` deep-link path (webapp/views/timeline.ts:246) opens the inspector and only THEN center-scrolls ("item 37 ordering"). SECOND SURFACE: the same rule applies to the Layer 1 Detail View drawer in task 257, which shrinks the timeline HORIZONTALLY rather than vertically — there the clicked node must center in the remaining left half, so the scroll is on the inline axis, not the block axis. Confirm with the user whether 258 covers both surfaces or only the existing webapp before implementing.

title: Layer 1 View: group same-timestamp nodes in a bubble behind a visual indicator
description: User request 2026-07-25, in their own wording: "visual indicator of some kind in the timeline bubble when two events happen at the same timestamp. maybe a rounded rectangle is put around the same-time nodes". WHY THIS IS REAL, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: a commit instant and a file's on-disk mtime routinely land on the SAME instant (a commit written and the working tree touched in the same second), and that tie is the mechanism behind the overprinting in specs/bug screenshots/'colliding filenames, commit nodes overlapping text.png' — `5636d8ec` drawn straight on top of `on disk`. Task 251 makes the tied nodes stop overlapping by giving each one its own row slot and charging the ruler for it, but once they are on separate rows NOTHING tells the reader they were simultaneous — the fix for the collision destroys the information. This task restores it: draw a rounded rectangle (or equivalent grouping affordance) around the run of nodes that share one instant, so the reader can see the rows are one moment rather than a sequence. The single tick that instant occupies on the ruler is the anchor the rectangle should read against. DESIGN REFERENCE: plans/layer1-mockup.html already computes exactly the grouping this needs — each node carries a `slot` index within its instant and `rowsAt` maps an instant to how many rows it needs; a run with `rowsAt > 1` is precisely a same-timestamp group. The fixture's README.md widget has a real tie (commit 4d5e6f70 and its mtime both at 2026-07-20T16:00:00Z), so the mockup can demonstrate the indicator without new test data. Implementation lands in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts plus the layer1.html style block.

title: Layer 1 View: clicking a ruler row centers that instant's bubble in the visible timeline area
description: User feature request 2026-07-25, in their own wording: "Click on a ruler row and the timeline bubble scrolls into the center of the visible timeline area." The ruler is the sticky left gutter in jfred/webapp/layer1.html; its rows are the per-instant ticks jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts renders from the `ruler` array the /api/layer1-view endpoint returns (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts). Today a tick is inert text — this makes it a navigation control. TARGET RULE, settled with the user 2026-07-25 when asked how to resolve a tick that several bubbles share: center the bubble that BEGINS at that instant (its first node is that tick), and — the user's words — "if no bubble starts there, scroll to the node at that timestamp". So the lookup is two-stage: (1) a pair widget whose first node sits on the clicked instant wins; (2) failing that, fall back to any node placed at that instant and center the bubble containing it. Center means the visible timeline area, so it must be measured AFTER any pane that shrinks the view has settled — see task 258, which is the same centering-against-post-reflow-layout requirement for the inspector, and task 257's Detail View drawer, which takes the right half. Must also stay correct under the zoom control (jfred/webapp/layer1-zoom.ts applies native CSS `zoom` to `.canvas`, so raw offsetTop/offsetLeft values are in unzoomed units while scrollTop/scrollLeft are not — the earlier zoom work already hit this class of bug). Give the ruler rows a pointer cursor and a hover state so they read as clickable.

title: Layer 1 View: add a jump-to-bubble text input so a named file can be scrolled to without hunting
description: Layer 1 View debugging affordance (user-directed 2026-07-25). Purpose: the agreed verification workflow is that Claude makes a visual change, names ONE bubble for the user to look at, and the user checks it by eye in their own running viewer — but the live jfred render is 808 widgets across ~156,000 px, so locating a named bubble by hand is the slow step that undermines the whole handoff. MECHANISM: a debugging text input in the layer1.html header. The user types a file name and the timeline viewport scrolls to that bubble. A `?focus=<path>` query parameter was considered and REJECTED by the user 2026-07-25: copying a long URL out of the CLI session's text output is HARDER than typing a value into a text box, so the deep link would not get used. Build the text box only — do not add the query param until something actually consumes it. Claude's side of the handoff is therefore to name a short value the user can TYPE, not a link to copy. REQUIREMENTS: (1) The input must accept what the user can SEE, which since task 245 is the BASENAME only — typing `launch.json` must work without the full `.vscode/launch.json`. (2) Basename collisions are common and must not be an error: this repo alone renders `.claude/launch.json`, `.vscode/launch.json`, `.vscode-parent/launch.json`, `tasks.json`, `.vscode/tasks.json` and `.vscode-parent/tasks.json`. Jump to the first match and provide a next-match affordance (repeat submit / Enter cycles to the next, wrapping) with a `2 of 6` style counter, so an ambiguous basename is navigable rather than rejected. Accepting a full or partial repo-relative path to narrow it is a bonus, not a substitute. (3) Scroll BOTH axes — a bubble is placed vertically by its earliest instant via margin-top and horizontally by its column index in .stage — and CENTRE the bubble in the pane rather than leaving it at an edge. (4) Briefly highlight the landed bubble so it is obvious which one was targeted. (5) Never a silent no-op: an unmatched name reports into the #crumb. (6) Account for the zoom control — offsetTop/offsetLeft inside the zoomed .canvas are unscaled, so verify the scroll lands correctly at a zoom other than 100%. CONSTRAINT: jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts is AT the repo's hard 250-line cap, so this needs its own module (jfred/webapp/layer1-focus.ts) in the same way layer1-zoom.ts and layer1-progress.ts were split out.
